BeanShotOut.description: One shot, judged against its band on the server, not in the browser.
BeanShotOut.title: BeanShotOut

ClicksReasonOut.description: The hard floor, or the softer warning line; both null when absent.
ClicksReasonOut.title: ClicksReasonOut

CoffeeDataOut.description:
The coffee the recipe is for -- the one deliberately loose model.

``POST /api/recommendation`` echoes back whatever ``coffee_data`` the client
sent and bag OCR's keys are not fixed, so unknown keys are kept and the
bean fields may be absent. Only the two keys the server always sets are
required.
CoffeeDataOut.title: CoffeeDataOut

CoffeeListOut.description: ``GET /api/logs``: the coffees, most recently brewed first.
CoffeeListOut.title: CoffeeListOut

EquipmentInput.description:
An equipment entry, and what the hardware can physically do.

The capabilities are all optional. Where the engine has no capability
data it abstains from recommending a value rather than guessing one, so a
blank field is a safe answer -- but spec_source should carry a citation
whenever the numbers are filled in, since an uncited capability row is a
guess.
EquipmentInput.title: EquipmentInput

FitShotOut.description: One shot of the history; ``index`` is what the pairs point at.
FitShotOut.title: FitShotOut

RecipeOut.description: Every number on the recipe card; all of them decided by the engine.
RecipeOut.title: RecipeOut

RecommendationRequest.description:
Ask for a recipe, either for a scanned bag or one already saved.

`bean_id` is what makes fine-tuning possible: the engine then works from
the real Bean row, so roast date and roast level are populated and the
resulting recommendation is stored against a real bean.
RecommendationRequest.title: RecommendationRequest

SuggestionOut.description: Cameron's use-less-coffee move, offered beside the recipe.
SuggestionOut.title: SuggestionOut

TargetOut.description: A target band, raw and as normalised time (time / brew ratio).
TargetOut.title: TargetOut

get.description:
Recent shots on one coffee, with each judged against its target.

The band verdict is computed here rather than in the browser because the
engine compares *normalised* time (time / brew ratio), not raw seconds.
Re-deriving that in JavaScript would drift from brewing.py the first time
the target bands change.
The grinder and brewer of the active setup, by name.

post.description: Log a shot. Returns the coffee's id, which is new on a bag's first shot.

get.description:
The working behind the current recommendation.

Read-only and model-free: it runs the same engine pass the recipe came
from with the prose switched off, so what it returns is the fit that
produced the number rather than a reconstruction that could disagree
with it. Nothing is persisted -- opening the view must not write a
recommendation row.
The user's coffees, most recently brewed first, each with its last shot.

post.description: Add a coffee by hand, with one shot on the active setup. All or nothing.

put.description: Edit a coffee and its latest shot (or give it one, if it has none).

post.description:
Regenerate the recipe for a scanned bag or a coffee already saved.

Called when the dose changes, when the active setup changes, and when the
user opens one of their existing coffees to fine-tune it. Passing
`bean_id` uses the stored row, so the engine sees the real roast date and
roast level rather than re-parsing strings, and the resulting
recommendation is recorded against that bean.

get.description:
What the server is currently serving.

The client compares this against the version its own bundle was loaded
with, so the user can tell whether a deploy actually reached their phone
or they are looking at a cached one.

Who the server thinks you are, and how it decided.

Deliberately the one user-scoped route that touches no database: when a
friend reports "it says I'm not signed in", this separates a Tailscale
identity problem (401 here) from an app problem (200 here, trouble
elsewhere) in a single request.
